A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Both have 25 pages; the appendices are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v4 reports original Gaussian-model simulations, hierarchical AR(1) experiments, and synthetic and real fluorescence lifetime imaging analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and their numerical results, including the appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The new Section 3.2 note recommends standard-normal initialization N(0,I) instead of the group-scaled latent initialization and states that damping is unnecessary for preventing divergence with an adaptive SDE solver under this modification. This revises sampling guidance while retaining the score networks, objectives, and hierarchical composition.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian toy task, hierarchical AR(1) grids, and synthetic and real fluorescence lifetime imaging data. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains the same samplers and GAUSS; Tables 2–3 retain their respective NUTS and direct ABI comparisons; the imaging experiments retain MLE and the non-hierarchical diffusion baseline.

E3.justification: The benchmark budgets, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, and sampling settings in Section 4 and Appendices A.4–A.8 are unchanged. The initialization recommendation is not accompanied by a revised benchmark protocol or identified rerun comparisons.

E4.justification: The damping, mini-batch, conditioning, and noise-schedule analyses in Figure 2 and Appendix Figures 5–8, together with the imaging diagnostics, are unchanged. The new note provides a qualitative reassessment without documenting an additional ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same repeated-run statements, median and median absolute deviation reporting, calibration diagnostics, and posterior predictive uncertainty displays. The new note adds no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. The new note adds a qualitative finding that standard-normal initialization substantially improves SDE stability and makes damping unnecessary for preventing divergence with an adaptive solver; no quantitative comparison accompanies it.

T1.justification: The numbered equations, posterior-factorization proof, mini-batch unbiasedness proof, and mathematical definitions remain unchanged. The new initialization recommendation has no accompanying derivation, revised proposition, or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable hierarchical inference and error-damping stabilization. These summaries are not revised to incorporate the qualification added in Section 3.2.

C2.justification: v4 attributes instability to compounding approximation errors and motivates damping as a stability remedy. v5 identifies latent-prior scaling as a primary practical cause and says standard initialization removes damping's necessity for avoiding divergence, while damping can still improve calibration. This substantially revises the causal explanation and role of a central component.

D1.justification: The note newly explains d(1)=1/J as compensation for prior scaling in the experiments and supplies explicit standard-normal initialization guidance. Architecture, training, hardware, solver tolerances, data processing, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The note specifically identifies the latent-prior scaling inherited from Geffner et al. (2023)'s annealed Langevin formulation as problematic for SDE sampling, refining the relationship to that prior method. The cited-work set and broader novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 inserts a short post-publication note in Section 3.2 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Existing prose and section order are retained; subsequent text shifts across page boundaries.

P2.justification: A shaded, bordered post-publication box is added on page 6, causing subsequent text and references to reflow and moving the conclusion from page 10 to page 11. Existing figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit correction improves transparency and practical guidance by acknowledging initialization's role and qualifying damping's necessity. The gain is limited: no new quantitative validation supports the recommendation, and the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the earlier stability narrative without integrating the correction.
